A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PhysSkin work, and all supplied text, equations, figures, and tables are readable. Neither PDF contains an appendix; both end with references. The additional page in v2 results from bibliography reflow.

before.justification: v1 reports original skinning evaluations on RigNet and ShapeNet, animation simulations, timing comparisons, and component ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original evaluations, simulation demonstrations, timing measurements, and ablation results in Section 4 and Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain identical subspace dynamics, neural skinning architecture, loss functions, normalization, and ConFIG optimization procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain ShapeNet and RigNet skinning evaluations, the deformable Lego shape family in Figure 8, and mesh and 3DGS animation demonstrations in Figures 9–11.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains RigNet, M-I-A, Anymate, and Puppeteer; Table 2 retains those methods plus Simplicits. FEM and MPM remain the timing comparators in Table 3, and qualitative comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 preserve the same training and testing procedures, preprocessing, sampling settings, three skinning metrics, and shared-hardware timing protocol.

E4.justification: Table 4 and Figure 12 contain the same normalization, ONI, ConFIG, and loss ablations. The training-evolution visualization and deformable-family case study are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and rankings in Tables 1–4 and qualitative results in Figures 3–12 are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains PhysSkin's log-condition number of 1.0453 and spectrum entropy of 0.9999.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 and their accompanying mathematical definitions and reasoning are identical, including the dynamics formulation, training objectives, and skinning metric definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain identical claims about geometry-only self-supervision, generalization across shapes and discretizations, and real-time physics-based animation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of generalization, numerical stability, physical consistency, and component contributions are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitation concerning the absence of semantic priors for complex geometries.

D1.justification: Architecture dimensions, point-sampling details, learning-rate schedule, four-RTX-4090 training hardware, and the project-page link remain identical. No implementation or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 57 works and retain identical related-work discussion and research positioning. Expanded venue names in v2 are bibliographic presentation edits, not changes in cited works.

P1.justification: v2 expands abbreviated bibliography venues, such as ACM TOG and Proc. of CVPR, into their full names and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Main-text wording and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Longer venue names alter bibliography line wrapping and column/page breaks, moving the end of reference 56 and reference 57 onto page 11. All twelve figures, four tables, captions, and main-text layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations are identical. Expanding venue names provides modest bibliographic clarification and causes reference reflow, without a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
